population: European, East Asian and African American ancestry cohorts
study_design: transcriptome-wide association, Mendelian randomization and colocalization across a 20-cohort longevity GWAS meta-analysis and GTEx v8 expression data
conclusion: Reports rs429358 as the shared causal variant colocalizing APOC1 and TOMM40 expression with survival beyond the 90th percentile (PP.H4 = 0.81 and 0.85), and states that this variant, the ApoE e4 site, is associated with a lower likelihood of longevity while rs7412 (ApoE e2) runs the other way.

population: Canadian Super Seniors (>=85, free of cancer, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, dementia and major pulmonary disease) versus mid-life controls
study_design: case-control genome-wide association study of 597 cases and 420 controls with candidate-variant and pathway analyses
conclusion: Confirms the known APOE association: APOE4 carriers had reduced odds of healthy aging (P = 0.0025), with a stronger effect in females (P = 8.82e-4).

study_design: bioinformatic and genomic analysis of variants associated with extreme human longevity
conclusion: Identifies the C allele of APOE rs7412 as the most prominent variant limiting extreme human longevity, which is the same axis read from the opposite allele.

population: European, East Asian and African American ancestry cohorts
study_design: transcriptome-wide association, Mendelian randomization and colocalization across a 20-cohort longevity GWAS meta-analysis and GTEx v8 expression data
conclusion: States that rs7412, the ApoE e2 variant, shows the opposite direction to the e4 variant rs429358, i.e. a higher likelihood of longevity.

population: Canadian Super Seniors (>=85, disease-free) versus mid-life controls
study_design: case-control genome-wide association study of 597 cases and 420 controls with candidate-variant and pathway analyses
conclusion: FOXO3 variants rs10457180, rs13217795 and rs2802292 showed nominal associations with increased odds of being a Super Senior, again primarily among females.

population: Southern Italian cohort affected by MASLD
study_design: observational association study of genotype against dietary intake
conclusion: Reports a protective effect of the FOXO3 rs2802292 G allele, the same allele carried by the longevity association, on food intake in this cohort.

population: European long-lived families (Leiden Longevity Study sibships)
study_design: affected sib-pair linkage analysis in 212 sibships enriched for ancestral longevity, followed by prioritisation of rare protein-altering variants inside the linked regions; bioRxiv preprint, not peer reviewed
conclusion: Identifies four linkage regions (1q21.1, 6p24.3, 6q14.3, 19p13.3) and prioritises 12 rare protein-altering variants in NUP210L, SLC27A3, CD1A, CGAS, IBTK, RARS2 and SH2D3A as candidates for familial longevity; the CGAS missense variant rs200818241 was found in two independent sibships and shown in cell models to reduce cGAS-STING signalling, mitigate inflammation and delay senescence.
